scope: Synthetic demonstration-group acceptance; unedited model output, not a site submission export

findings.what_student_wrote: I handle two different students competing for the final course seat. I put the seat-count change and the enrollment insert in one database transaction. I use a conditional update: UPDATE courses SET remaining = remaining - 1 WHERE course_id = ? AND remaining > 0. Only one affected row means that this request reserved a seat. Zero affected rows means no seat was reserved, so I reject the request. I then insert enrollment and commit the two changes together. If the insert or either operation fails, I roll back every change in this transaction, including the reserved seat. I do not use an explicit SELECT FOR UPDATE lock; the successful conditional write protects the shared capacity. Cached availability makes browsing faster but can be stale. Cached values never authorize enrollment: the database conditional update is the final authority.

The approaches are conceptually equivalent in their handling of concurrency and rollback mechanisms.
